key_insight: AVGen-Bench is a task-driven, multi-granular benchmark that evaluates text-to-audio-video (T2AV) systems for fine-grained joint correctness of audio and video, going beyond isolated or coarse embedding-based metrics to capture realistic prompt requirements.
problem_solved: Current T2AV evaluation is fragmented: audio and video are often measured separately or by coarse embedding similarity, which misses temporal alignment, event-level correspondence, and nuanced multimodal errors required for real-world prompts.
method: Curate high-quality, realistic prompts spanning 11 real-world categories to drive evaluation toward functional tasks.
Define a multi-granular evaluation protocol that measures clip-level fidelity, event/frame-level correctness, temporal alignment, and audio–visual correspondence.
Combine automated metric suite with targeted task-driven tests and human judgments to produce robust, interpretable scores for joint T2AV quality.
impact: Provides researchers and practitioners a standardized, fine-grained way to compare and diagnose T2AV systems, accelerating progress on models that must satisfy both audio and visual correctness in realistic use cases.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: prompt → T2AV model(s) → multi-granular metric suite (clip/event/frame/alignment) → composite score
Side-by-side examples: sample prompt with generated audio+video and annotated success/failure points (e.g., missing sound event, misaligned action)
Metric comparison chart: coarse embedding similarity vs. AVGen-Bench multi-granular scores showing divergence on realistic prompts
Heatmap or stacked bars: per-category performance across the 11 real-world categories to highlight strengths/weaknesses
paper_title: AVGen-Bench: A Task-Driven Benchmark for Multi-Granular Evaluation of Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
paper_authors: Ziwei Zhou, Zeyuan Lai, Rui Wang, Yifan Yang, Zhen Xing
